name: Landscape Connections
summary: A GBP 150 million initiative for about 20 long-term nature-recovery projects in UK Protected Landscapes, led by not-for-profits or partnerships they lead, with grants up to GBP 10 million.
reporting: Grantees must measure the project's impact on nature recovery and on engaging people, using government outcomes frameworks where they exist.

steps: Committee recommendation and Board of Trustees decision

eligibility.rule: Project has an area of designated Protected Landscape at its core (flexible in Scotland)
Demonstrating greater public benefit than private gain when private or for-profit organisations are involved
Includes the relevant Protected Landscape management body as a key partner where works take place
Project delivery phase lasts no more than eight years

status.quote: You can apply for a grant up to £10m through our National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10m.

applicant_types.quote: Applications are open to not-for-profit organisations, and partnerships led by not-for-profit organisations, from across the UK.

geography.quote: Applications are open to not-for-profit organisations, and partnerships led by not-for-profit organisations, from across the UK.

access.quote: For grants over £250,000 you must first submit an Expression of Interest.

amount.quote: You can apply for a grant up to £10m through our National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10m.

co_finance_required.quote: Our funding will cover a percentage of the overall project costs with the balance provided through partnership or match funding.

reporting.quote: Allocate resources to measuring the impact of your project for both nature recovery and engaging people

effort.quote: £10,000 to £250,000: you can use our optional Project Enquiry to get feedback within 10 working days. £250,000 to £10m: you must submit an Expression of Interest before starting a full funding application.
If your Expression of Interest is successful, you will then submit a development phase application.
If your development phase application is successful, you will receive funding and have up to two years to develop a detailed project proposal for your delivery phase application.
12noon, 25 February 2027, to receive a decision by end of June 2027
For grants above £250,000, recommendations will be made by nation/area committees, with final decisions made on a quarterly basis by our Board of Trustees.

eligibility.quote: have an area of designated Protected Landscape at its core although flexibility will apply in Scotland
If private owners or for-profit organisations are involved in the project, we expect public benefit to be demonstrably greater than private gain.

Protected Landscape management bodies must be a key partner within any application relating to the landscape where they operate and where the works will be taking place, though they do not need to be the applicant or lead partner of an application.
Your project delivery phase can last for up to eight years

co_finance.quote: For grant requests between £250,000 and £1m: You must provide at least 5% of the costs of the development phase and at least 5% of the costs of the delivery phase as partnership funding. For grant requests between £1m and £10m: You must provide at least 10% of the costs of the development phase and at least 10% of the costs of the delivery phase as partnership funding.

after_award.quote: Over the life of your delivery phase, you will need to submit: a project update every three months a separate yearly project update once a year a final project update and completion report when you complete your project
